column1: # The locks that src/ takes, checked by scripts/check-locks.sh (lint). Tab-separated:
#   file, function, call, mode, n (acquisitions of that call and mode in the function), object, scope, longest hold, the lock core PostgreSQL takes for the same kind of work, verdict.

# "same" in the verdict: the mode and the hold are no stronger or longer than PostgreSQL's. Anything else says what it conflicts with and why. Opens at AccessShareLock, RowExclusiveLock and NoLock need no row.
# scripts/check-locks.sh --list prints the acquisitions found, to copy a new row from. A lock that holds INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/SELECT out for longer than O(page) is a defect, not a row to add.
